def-cm13-two-form.physical_scope: The symplectic data of a potential presentation of the framework's force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart $Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ the canonical one-form $\lambda=p\cdot\delta x$ and the two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the forms pulled back along the presentation's own chart map $(q,P)\mapsto(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$. The item defines model objects of the declared presentation and its declared chart only; it asserts no closedness, nondegeneracy, dynamics or measured value, and it fixes the sign convention $\iota_X\omega=dH$ used throughout this page.

def-cm13-two-form:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$,
a $C^{2}$ potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], the Euclidean product on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Write $n:=3N\ge1$. The
Cartesian momentum phase chart of the presentation is
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with the momentum $p=\mathsf Mv$ of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], and the momentum phase chart of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates is
$I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ with the generalized momentum
$P=G(q)v$, $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]).

**(a) Cartesian chart.** The **Cartesian phase domain of the presentation** is
the nonempty open set

$$W:=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n},\qquad z=(x,p),$$

a phase domain in the sense of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]
(openness is clause (a) of [[def-cm01-configuration]]). On $W$ the
**canonical one-form of the presentation in the Cartesian chart** is the smooth
one-form

$$\lambda_{(x,p)}(\delta x,\delta p):=p\cdot\delta x\qquad\bigl((x,p)\in W,\ (\delta x,\delta p)\in\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N}\bigr),$$

where $p\cdot\delta x$ is the Euclidean pairing of the momentum covector with
the displacement, and the **two-form of the presentation in the Cartesian
chart** is

$$\omega:=-d\lambda$$

([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]). In coordinates, reading
$x=(x^{1},\dots,x^{3N})$ and $p=(p_{1},\dots,p_{3N})$ as the standard
coordinates of $W$,

$$\lambda=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}p_{a}\,dx^{a},\qquad \omega=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a},\qquad \omega_{(x,p)}\bigl((\delta x,\delta p),(\delta x',\delta p')\bigr)=\delta x\cdot\delta p'-\delta p\cdot\delta x',$$

the last identity using the Euclidean product. The dimension of both forms is
that of action, $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$: the pairing of a momentum
($\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$) with a displacement ($\ell$). The forms have no
explicit time dependence; for each $t\in I_{0}$ the slice $\{t\}\times W$
carries the same two-form. The momentum phase chart with time,
$I_{0}\times W$ with coordinates $(t,x,p)$, is the domain of the Hamiltonians
and fields of this page. The **sign convention** fixed by
[[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]] and used
throughout is $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$; $H$ denotes a phase function as in that
item.

**(b) Generalized-coordinate chart.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$ and
kinetic metric $G$, and let $r$ be its number of coordinates
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). The **chart map of the
presentation in the coordinates $X$** is

$$\Phi_{X}:\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Phi_{X}(q,P):=\Bigl(X(q),\ \mathsf M\,DX(q)\,G(q)^{-1}P\Bigr).$$

Here $DX(q)$ is the $(3N)\times r$ Jacobian of $X$ at $q$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
is symmetric positive definite ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]],
[[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), and $P$ is a
generalized momentum. The image of $\Phi_{X}$ is

$$\Phi_{X}(\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r})=\bigl\{\,(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)v)\ :\ q\in\Omega,\ v\in\mathbb R^{r}\,\bigr\},$$

the momentum chart of the presentation in the coordinates $X$; indeed
$P\mapsto v=G(q)^{-1}P$ is a linear bijection of $\mathbb R^{r}$. The map
$\Phi_{X}$ is $C^{1}$ by the displayed algebra, and it is a $C^{1}$ immersion:
its derivative is injective at every point, because $DX(q)$ is injective
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-euclidean-submersions-and-immersions]]) and $P\mapsto G(q)^{-1}P$ is a
linear bijection; when $r=3N$ its derivative is invertible and it is a local
diffeomorphism onto $W$
(equivalently $\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$: see the
recorded identity below). The **forms of the presentation in the
coordinates $X$** are the pullbacks

$$\lambda_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda,\qquad \omega_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$$

([[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]). In the coordinates $(q,P)$ on
$\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ the following identities hold, and are proved in
clause 2 of the symplectic-structure theorem of this page:

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

moreover, when $r=3N$ and $DX(q)$ is invertible,
$\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$, so that on an open
generalized-coordinate chart the chart map reads
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=\bigl(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}P\bigr)$ and the chart
transition between the two descriptions of the same momentum datum is a
$C^{1}$ local diffeomorphism.

**(c) Status.** The item defines the two-form datum of the declared
presentation on its declared charts, together with the sign convention for
fields. It asserts no closedness, no nondegeneracy, no equation of motion, no
conservation law and no measured value; those are the subject of the other
items of this page. The forms depend on the declared chart and its coordinate
dimensions, but not on the residual forces $d$ nor on the normalization
$U\mapsto U+c(t)$ of the potential representative. All objects are model
objects of the idealization declared by the force branch.

pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic.physical_scope: The symplectic structure of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart the two-form $\omega=\sum dx^a\wedge dp_a$ is closed and nondegenerate, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the pullback of the presentation's two-form along the presentation's own chart map has the canonical coordinate expression. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no dynamics, no conservation law and no measured value.

pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and forms of [[def-cm13-two-form]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$,
open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian phase
domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $n=3N$, its canonical one-form
$\lambda$ and two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and for each generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates and kinetic metric $G$ the chart map
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$ with pullbacks
$\lambda_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda$ and $\omega_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). Then:

1. **(Cartesian chart)** $\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase
   domain $W$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]: $d\omega=0$ and
   $\omega$ is nondegenerate at every point of $W$; hence $(W,\omega)$ is a
   symplectic manifold in the sense of
   [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]].
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** On $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$,

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

   consequently $\omega_{X}$ is closed and nondegenerate at every point, so
   $\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase domain
   $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and $\Phi_{X}$ preserves the two-form.
3. **(chart independence)** Where two of the presentation's charts are
   defined and overlap, the transition between them preserves the two-form,
   and the difference of their canonical one-forms is closed: any two
   momentum charts of the presentation describe the same symplectic
   structure on the overlap, up to the closed one-form $\lambda$ gauge.

The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the cited mathematics. It asserts no equation of
motion, no conservation law, no completeness of any flow and no empirical
content.

def-cm13-canonical-form.physical_scope: The vocabulary of canonical coordinates for the two-form of a declared potential presentation: coordinates on a phase domain in which the presentation's two-form takes the canonical coordinate expression, and the record that the presentation's Cartesian momentum chart and each of its generalized-coordinate momentum charts are canonical charts. The item defines a coordinate condition and fixes the vocabulary used by the bracket, field, flow and generating-function items; it asserts no dynamics, no existence of canonical coordinates beyond the model's own charts and no measured value.

def-cm13-canonical-form:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts, the phase domains and the two-form datum of
[[def-cm13-two-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with $n=3N$, its two-form $\omega$, and for each generalized-coordinate map
$X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates the chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form
$\omega_{X}$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]). All
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Canonical coordinates.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ (or
$W_{0}\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$) be nonempty open, and let

$$\theta=(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m}):W_{0}\longrightarrow V\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m}$$

be a $C^{1}$ chart of $W_{0}$ onto an open set $V$ ([[def-metric-topology]]),
with $m$ the half-dimension of $W_{0}$. The coordinates $\theta$ are
**canonical coordinates for the presentation's two-form** on $W_{0}$ when the
two-form takes the **canonical form**

$$\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{m}d\theta^{a}\wedge d\theta^{m+a}$$

pointwise on $W_{0}$, using the finite-coordinate form and pullback conventions of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]; equivalently, when the
pullback identity $\theta^{*}\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}=\omega|_{W_{0}}$ holds
for the standard two-form $\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}$ of $V$
([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]],
[[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]), equivalently when
$D\theta(z)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\theta(z)=J$ for the standard symplectic matrix
$J$ at every $z\in W_{0}$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]). A **canonical
chart of the presentation** is a chart whose coordinates are canonical in
this sense; the equivalence with the canonical maps defined later on this
page is recorded with those definitions.

**(b) The model's own charts are canonical.** The Cartesian coordinates
$(x,p)$ on $W$ are canonical coordinates: by clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the two-form is
$\omega=\sum_{a}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$. For a generalized-coordinate map, the
coordinates $(q,P)$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ are canonical coordinates
for the pulled-back form $\omega_{X}$: by clause 2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] one has
$\omega_{X}=\sum_{a}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a}$, and when the map is a genuine chart
($r=3N$) the chart transition is a change of canonical coordinates on
overlaps.

**(c) Canonical one-form up to gauge at classical differentiability.** For a $C^2$ canonical chart $\theta$, the canonical one-form $\lambda$ of
[[def-cm13-two-form]] is said to be **in canonical form up to gauge** in the
canonical coordinates $\theta$ when the difference
$\lambda-\sum_{a}\theta^{m+a}d\theta^{a}$ is a closed one-form on $W_{0}$;
exactness of that difference is not required. For the presentation's own
charts the difference of the two canonical one-forms is closed by clause 3 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]. These charts are $C^2$ or smoother. For a merely $C^1$ chart clause (a) retains its full pointwise meaning, but the coefficients of the pulled-back one-form may be only continuous, so this clause does not apply the classical exterior derivative to them.

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines a coordinate condition on a
declared chart and records the one fact that the presentation's own momentum
charts satisfy it. It asserts no existence of canonical coordinates beyond
the model's charts, no global statement on multiply connected phase domains,
no dynamics and no measured value. A chart that is merely a diffeomorphism
need not be canonical; the determinant test
$|\det D\theta|=1$ is necessary but, in dimension $2m\ge4$, not sufficient
for canonicity (the scope remark of this page records the witness).

def-cm13-hamiltonian-field.physical_scope: The Hamiltonian field datum of a declared potential presentation: for a $C^{2}$ phase function the unique $C^{1}$ field contracted against the presentation's two-form to the differential, together with its coordinate expression in the model's Cartesian and generalized-coordinate charts and its specialization to the branch Hamiltonian, including the residual-force source that is generally not a Hamiltonian field. The item defines model fields and their chart expressions; it asserts no existence of integral curves, no equation of motion and no measured value.

def-cm13-hamiltonian-field:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, its two-form $\omega$, a generalized-coordinate
chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form $\omega_{X}$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]); the presentation is
hyperregular on every chart with the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],

$$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x),\qquad \widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12\,P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q).$$

Differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and gradients those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].

**(a) The field of a phase function.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ be nonempty
open and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$. By clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the form $\omega$ is nondegenerate on
$W_{0}$, so there is exactly one $C^{1}$ vector field $X_{f}$ on $W_{0}$ with

$$\iota_{X_{f}}\omega=df$$

(the sign convention of [[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]]
and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]); it
is the **Hamiltonian field of $f$ for the presentation**. In the Cartesian
coordinates $(x,p)$, writing $\nabla f=(f_{x^{1}},\dots,f_{x^{3N}},f_{p_{1}},\dots,f_{p_{3N}})$,

$$X_{f}=\bigl(f_{p},\,-f_{x}\bigr)=J\nabla f,\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0_{3N}&I_{3N}\\-I_{3N}&0_{3N}\end{pmatrix};$$

in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of the presentation
the same field reads $X_{f}=\bigl(f_{\theta^{m+1}},\dots,f_{\theta^{2m}},-f_{\theta^{1}},\dots,-f_{\theta^{m}}\bigr)$.
A vector field on $W_{0}$ is called **Hamiltonian for the presentation** when
it is $X_{f}$ for some $C^{2}$ function $f$; in particular
$X_{f}=0$ exactly when $f$ is locally constant on $W_{0}$. Vector fields are
read as tangent-bundle sections of
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]].

**(b) The field of the branch Hamiltonian.** For each $t\in I_{0}$ the
function $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ is $C^{2}$ on $W$, and the **Hamiltonian field
of the presentation** at time $t$ is $X_{H_{t}}$:

$$X_{H_{t}}(x,p)=\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,\ -\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\bigr),$$

whose components are a velocity and a force. In the coordinates $X$ the
corresponding field is
$X_{\widetilde H_{t}}(q,P)=\bigl(G(q)^{-1}P,\ -\partial_{q}\widetilde H(t,q,P)\bigr)$,
where the second slot retains the kinetic contribution
$-\tfrac12P\cdot\partial_{q}(G(q)^{-1})P$ when the metric varies. If
$d\not\equiv0$ the model's forced evolution carries the additional momentum
source $d$; the corresponding vector field
$(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
is generally not a Hamiltonian field for the presentation, and it is one
exactly when the residual force has a potential independent of the velocity
slot (the criterion is proved in clause 4 of the corresponding theorem of this
page).

**(c) Time dependence and status.** For a time-dependent $H$ the assignment
$t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$ is a time-dependent field on the phase domain; each
$X_{H_{t}}$ is $C^{1}$, hence locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and no
completeness of its integral curves is asserted here. The item defines the
field datum and its chart expressions; the identification of the model's
motions with the integral curves, and all conservation or invariance
properties, are the subject of the other items of this page. The field is
defined by the intrinsic equation $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$ and therefore does not
depend on the canonical chart used to compute it.

pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-t.physical_scope: The identification of the model's Hamiltonian evolution with the integral curves of the presentation's Hamiltonian field: on the potential branch the model's motions, the solutions of Hamilton's equations for the branch Hamiltonian and the integral curves of $X_H$ coincide, and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart the declared Lagrange equations coincide with the corresponding Hamilton system; with residual forces the momentum equation carries the force as a source, and the forced field is Hamiltonian exactly when that source derives from a velocity-independent potential. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it makes no existence, uniqueness, completeness or empirical claim.

pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-t:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and Hamiltonian field of [[def-cm13-two-form]],
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and open
configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian
Hamiltonian $H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ and, for a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with kinetic metric
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX$, the chart Hamiltonian
$\widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q)$
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open
interval. Then:

1. **(potential branch, Cartesian chart)** Assume $d\equiv0$ on the state
   domain. For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$ with $p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$ the
   following are equivalent: (a) $x$ is a motion of the model
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]); (b) $\dot x(t)=H_{p}(t,x(t),p(t))$ and
   $\dot p(t)=-H_{x}(t,x(t),p(t))$ for every $t\in J$; (c) the curve
   $t\mapsto(x(t),p(t))$ is an integral curve of the time-dependent field
   $t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$, i.e. satisfies
   $\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$ with $z=(x,p)$
   ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]).
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
   generalized-coordinate map and let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
   $x:=X\circ q$ and $P(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then the declared Lagrange
   equations with residual generalized force,
   $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$, are
   equivalent to
   $q'(t)=\widetilde H_{P}(t,q(t),P(t))$ and
   $P'(t)=-\widetilde H_{q}(t,q(t),P(t))+Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$;
   in particular, when $d\equiv0$, they are equivalent to
   $(q,P)$ being an integral curve of $X_{\widetilde H_{t}}$.
3. **(residual forces, Cartesian chart)** For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$
   with $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the model's forced equation
   $\mathsf Mx''=-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,x')$ holds on $J$ if and only if
   $\dot x=H_{p}$ and $\dot p=-H_{x}+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)$ on $J$.
4. **(when is the forced field Hamiltonian?)** The forced field
   $(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
   is the Hamiltonian field of a $C^{2}$ phase function on its domain if and
   only if there is a $C^{2}$ function $V:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ with
   $d(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x}V(t,x)$ for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; in
   that case the phase function is $H+V$ up to an independently chosen
   additive $C^2$ function of $t$ on each connected component of $Q$, and the model's forced motions are the motions of the potential
   presentation $(U+V,0)$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the declared chart; it asserts no existence or uniqueness of
solutions, no completeness, no conservation law and no empirical content.

def-cm13-poisson.physical_scope: The pointwise bracket is defined for C1 inputs, with the C2 intrinsic-field expression and C1 output regularity retained. The Poisson bracket datum of a declared potential presentation: phase functions read off the labels' positions and momenta, the bracket $\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)$ defined by the presentation's two-form, and its coordinate formula in the model's Cartesian and generalized-coordinate canonical charts. The item defines a model bilinear operation and fixes its dimension; it asserts no algebraic identity, no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value.

def-cm13-poisson:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] and the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]. Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]];
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Phase functions.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of a phase
domain of the presentation. A **phase function of the presentation on
$W_{0}$ of class $C^{k}$** is a map $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k}$
($k\ge1$); its physical reading is a model quantity computed from the
positions and momenta of the labels, and its dimension is declared as part of
the datum. A **time-dependent phase function** on an interval $J\subseteq
I_{0}$ is a map $f:J\times W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of the declared class, written
$f_{t}:=f(t,\cdot)$.

**(b) The bracket.** For $C^1$ phase functions $f,g:W_0\to\mathbb R$, define their **Poisson bracket for the presentation** by the pointwise coordinate formula $\{f,g\}=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\nabla g$ in a canonical chart, in the finite-regularity convention of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]. This is a continuous function. The definition is independent of the canonical chart: for a canonical $C^1$ coordinate change with derivative $M$, the matrix identity implies $MJM^{\mathsf T}=J$, and the equivalence of the two matrix identities is proved in [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]], and the chain rule transforms the two gradients so their pairing is unchanged.

When both functions are $C^2$, their Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] are $C^1$, and the bracket has the intrinsic formula
$$\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)=df(X_g)=X_g(f)=-X_f(g).$$
In this case it is $C^1$, with the same sign convention as the smooth root bracket and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]. The extension to $C^1$ inputs makes evolution identities for $C^1$ observables and nested brackets of $C^2$ functions meaningful; it does not assert closure of the $C^2$ class under the bracket. Its dimension is $[f][g](\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1})^{-1}$, the product of the entries' dimensions divided by the action dimension of the two-form.

**(c) Coordinate formula.** In the Cartesian canonical coordinates $(x,p)$
of the presentation, and more generally in any canonical chart
$(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]],

$$\{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}\Bigl(f_{x^{a}}g_{p_{a}}-f_{p_{a}}g_{x^{a}}\Bigr)=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g,\qquad \{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{m}\Bigl(f_{\theta^{a}}g_{\theta^{m+a}}-f_{\theta^{m+a}}g_{\theta^{a}}\Bigr),$$

with derivatives those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. The coordinate formula is
recorded here and its identities (bilinearity, skew-symmetry, the Leibniz
rule, the Jacobi identity and the fundamental brackets) are proved in the
bracket-identities theorem of this page.

**(d) Status.** The item defines a bilinear operation on the declared phase
domain by the pointwise coordinate formula, and for $C^2$ entries by $\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)$, hence
independently of the canonical chart used to evaluate the coordinate
formula. It asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no algebraic
identity beyond well-definedness and no measured value; in particular the
bracket with the Hamiltonian and the notion of first integral are the subject
of the evolution theorem of this page.

pthm-cm13-bracket-identities.physical_scope: The algebraic identities of the Poisson bracket of a declared potential presentation: bilinearity, skew-symmetry, the Leibniz rule in each slot, the Jacobi identity for $C^{2}$ phase functions through the pointwise C1-slot extension, the smooth Poisson algebra, the identity $\{f,g\}=X_g(f)$ relating the bracket to the presentation's Hamiltonian fields, and the fundamental brackets of the model's canonical coordinates. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value.

pthm-cm13-bracket-identities:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the bracket of [[def-cm13-poisson]] on a
nonempty open subset $W_{0}$ of a phase domain of the presentation. Then:

1. **(bilinearity and skew-symmetry)** The bracket is real-bilinear:
   $\{\alpha f+\beta g,h\}=\alpha\{f,h\}+\beta\{g,h\}$ and
   $\{f,\alpha g+\beta h\}=\alpha\{f,g\}+\beta\{f,h\}$ for real $\alpha,\beta$
   and $C^{2}$ phase functions; it is skew-symmetric,
   $\{f,g\}=-\{g,f\}$, and in particular $\{f,f\}=0$.
2. **(Leibniz rule)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g,h$,

$$\{f,gh\}=\{f,g\}h+g\{f,h\},\qquad \{fg,h\}=f\{g,h\}+g\{f,h\}.$$

3. **(Jacobi identity)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g,h$,

$$\{f,\{g,h\}\}+\{g,\{h,f\}\}+\{h,\{f,g\}\}=0.$$

4. **(relation to the fields)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g$ one has
   $\{f,g\}=X_{g}(f)=-X_{f}(g)=d\!f(X_{g})=-d\!g(X_{f})$, and the bracket is
   $C^{1}$; in the Cartesian canonical coordinates
   $\{f,g\}=\sum_{a}(f_{x^{a}}g_{p_{a}}-f_{p_{a}}g_{x^{a}})=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g$,
   and in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ the analogous
   formula of [[def-cm13-poisson]] clause (c) holds.
5. **(fundamental brackets)** In the Cartesian canonical coordinates the
   coordinate functions satisfy $\{x^{a},x^{b}\}=0$, $\{p_{a},p_{b}\}=0$ and
   $\{x^{a},p_{b}\}=\delta^{a}_{b}$; more generally, in any canonical chart
   $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ one has
   $\{\theta^{i},\theta^{j}\}=J^{ij}$, the entries of the standard symplectic
   matrix.

For nested brackets use the pointwise $C^1$-slot coordinate extension of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]], which agrees with the presentation bracket on $C^2$ inputs. Thus the Jacobi identity above is meaningful for $C^2$ functions despite their brackets being only $C^1$. The $C^2$ class is not in general closed under the bracket and is not asserted to be a Poisson algebra. The smooth $C^\infty$ phase functions, equipped with this bracket and pointwise product, form a Poisson algebra.
The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no
conservation law and no measured value.

pthm-cm13-observable-evolution.physical_scope: The evolution identity of the declared potential presentation: along the model's Hamiltonian solutions the total time derivative of a phase function is its explicit time derivative plus the bracket with the branch Hamiltonian; autonomous functions with vanishing bracket are constant on trajectories, and, for an autonomous Hamiltonian, the bracket of two autonomous $C^{3}$ first integrals is again a first integral and the Hamiltonian itself is a first integral. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content.

pthm-cm13-observable-evolution:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the Hamiltonian
fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$, assumed of class $C^{2}$
in $(t,z)$ on $I_{0}\times W$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open interval and
let $z:J\to W$ be a $C^{1}$ solution of the Hamiltonian system
$\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$, equivalently, on the potential branch with
$z=(x,p)$ and $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the momentum-phase curve of a motion of the
model ([[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]],
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]],
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]). Then:

1. **(evolution identity)** For every $C^{1}$ phase function
   $f:U\to\mathbb R$ on an open set $U$ containing the graph of $z$,
   $t\mapsto f(t,z(t))$ is differentiable on $J$ and

$$\frac{d}{dt}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)=\partial_{t}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)+\{f_{t},H_{t}\}\bigl(z(t)\bigr),$$

   where $f_{t}:=f(t,\cdot)$, $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ and the bracket is that of
   [[def-cm13-poisson]].
2. **(first integrals)** If $f$ is autonomous and
   $\{f,H_{t}\}(z(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$, then $f\circ z$ is constant on
   $J$; in particular, if in addition $H$ is autonomous
   ($\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ and $d\equiv0$), then $H$ itself is constant
   along $z$, the Hamiltonian form of the energy conservation of
   [[pthm-cm12-energy-time]].
3. **(closed algebra)** Let $H$ be autonomous and let $f,g$ be autonomous
   $C^{3}$ phase functions with $\{f,H\}=0$ and $\{g,H\}=0$ everywhere on
   their common domain. Then $\{f,g\}$ is again a first integral of $H$:
   $\{\{f,g\},H\}=0$ everywhere, and $\{f,g\}$ is constant along every
   solution of the Hamiltonian system on which it is defined.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and
no existence, uniqueness or completeness of solutions.

def-cm13-canonical-map.physical_scope: The canonical-map datum of a declared potential presentation: $C^{1}$ maps between open subsets of the presentation's phase domains which pull the two-form back to itself, the determinant test on their Jacobians, the transport identity for Hamiltonian fields, and the record that the model's chart transitions, flow maps and generating-function maps are canonical. The item defines the model's canonical transformations and fixes the tests used throughout this page and by its consumers; it asserts no existence of canonical maps beyond the listed suppliers and no measured value.

def-cm13-canonical-map:
## Definition

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] and the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Let $W_{1},W_{2}$ be nonempty open subsets
of phase domains of the presentation, carrying the two-forms
$\omega_{1},\omega_{2}$ of [[def-cm13-two-form]] (for a generalized-coordinate
chart this is the pulled-back form $\omega_{X}$ in the coordinates $(q,P)$).

**(a) Canonical maps.** A $C^{1}$ map $C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ is a **canonical map
of the presentation** when

$$C^{*}\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}$$

on $W_{1}$ ([[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]); it is a **canonical
transformation** when in addition $C$ is a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism onto
$W_{2}$. This is the finite-regularity convention of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]. In the smooth subcase it agrees with [[def-canonical-transformation]] and [[def-symplectomorphism-local-symplectomorphism-and-symplectic-embedding]]; a merely $C^1$ map is not asserted to satisfy their smoothness hypothesis.

**(b) Tests.** By
[[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]] clause 1, applied
in canonical coordinates on $W_{1}$ and $W_{2}$, a $C^{1}$ map
$C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ is canonical if and only if

$$DC(z)^{\mathsf T}J\,DC(z)=J\qquad\text{for every }z\in W_{1},$$

so in particular a canonical map is a local diffeomorphism, its derivative
being invertible at every point and the $C^1$ inverse function theorem supplying a local inverse
([[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]], [[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]],
[[cor-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-is-a-unit]]); and a canonical
$C^{1}$ diffeomorphism satisfies $|\det DC(z)|=1$ for every $z$
([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]). In dimension $2m\ge4$ the condition
$|\det DC|=1$ alone is strictly weaker than canonicity (the companion page
carries an explicit volume-preserving, non-canonical shear), while for $m=1$ the symplectic condition is exactly $\det DC=1$; absolute determinant $1$ alone also admits orientation-reversing, antisymplectic maps.

**(c) Elementary closure and transport.** By functoriality of the pullback
(the pointwise chain-rule pullback of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]), the
identity map, composites of canonical maps and inverses of canonical
transformations are canonical; and for a $C^{2}$ canonical map
$C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ and a $C^{2}$ function $f$ on $W_{2}$ the Hamiltonian
fields satisfy

$$DC(z)\,X_{f\circ C}(z)=X_{f}\bigl(C(z)\bigr)\qquad(z\in W_{1}),$$

so that $C$ conjugates the Hamiltonian system of $f$ to that of $f\circ C$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]] clause 3). The
consequences — preservation of brackets, transport of solutions, preservation
of volume — are proved in the transport and volume items of this page.

**(d) The model's canonical maps.** The following maps of the presentation
are canonical: the chart transition $\Phi_{X}$ between the Cartesian and a
generalized-coordinate momentum chart, and the transition between two such
charts (clause 3 of [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]); the time-slice
maps of the Hamiltonian evolution of any $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian, proved
in the flow-preservation theorem of this page; the local maps generated by
first- and second-kind generating functions, proved in the
generating-function theorem of this page; and
the drift, kick and velocity-Verlet maps of the mechanical splitting in exact
arithmetic ([[prop-cm-drift-kick-and-verlet-preserve-the-canonical-form]]).

**(e) Status.** The item defines the canonical maps of the presentation and
fixes the two equivalent tests of clause (b). It asserts no existence of a
canonical map beyond the listed suppliers, no global statement on multiply
connected phase domains and no empirical content; in particular, canonicity
is a local condition on the two-form, and a canonical map need not admit a
globally defined real generating function, as the scope remark of this page
records.

pthm-cm13-flow-preservation.physical_scope: Preservation of the symplectic structure by the model's Hamiltonian evolution: on the actual time-slice domains of a $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian, also for a time-dependent Hamiltonian, the solution map is a canonical map of the presentation, preserves the bracket of $C^{2}$ phase functions and has unit determinant; hence the model's potential-branch flow preserves the presentation's two-form locally in time. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; no completeness of the flow, no all-time assertion and no measured value is claimed.

pthm-cm13-flow-preservation:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the Hamiltonian field of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]: the Cartesian Hamiltonian
$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ of class $C^{2}$ on
$I_{0}\times W$, where the potential $U$ and the residual forces $d$ are
those of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and the data are those of
[[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm01-units]]
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]). Let
$t_{0}\in I_{0}$ and $z_{0}\in W$. Then there are reals $h>0$, $\rho>0$ and
an open neighbourhood $U_{0}\subseteq W$ of $z_{0}$ such that:

1. **(solution map)** the solutions $t\mapsto\Phi(t;y)$ of the Hamiltonian
   system $\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$ through $y\in U_{0}$ at time $t_{0}$
   are defined for $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$, and the solution map
   $\Phi:[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]\times U_{0}\to W$ is $C^{1}$ in $y$; for each
   fixed $t$ the time-$t$ map $\Phi_{t}:=\Phi(t;\cdot)$ is a canonical map of
   the presentation on $U_{0}$:

$$D\Phi_{t}(y)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\Phi_{t}(y)=J,\qquad \Phi_{t}^{*}\omega=\omega\qquad(y\in U_{0}),$$

   and $\det D\Phi_{t}(y)=1$ for every $y\in U_{0}$.
2. **(bracket preservation)** For every $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$ and all
   $C^{2}$ phase functions $f,g$ on $W$,
   $\{f\circ\Phi_{t},\,g\circ\Phi_{t}\}=\{f,g\}\circ\Phi_{t}$ on $U_{0}$.
3. **(potential branch)** On the potential branch ($d\equiv0$) the curves
   $t\mapsto\Phi(t;y)$ are, through
   [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]], the
   momentum-phase curves of the model's motions, so the model's Hamiltonian
   evolution preserves the presentation's two-form, bracket and determinant
   on the actual time-slice domains; the assertion is local in time, and no
   completeness of the flow is claimed.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics. It requires no autonomy of $H$: the
conclusion holds for each fixed pair of times on which the solutions exist.

pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canon.physical_scope: Transformation theory for the declared potential presentation: a $C^{2}$ canonical map conjugates the Hamiltonian field of a phase function to the field of the composed function, preserves the model's Poisson bracket under composition, and carries solutions of one Hamiltonian system to solutions of the other, also for time-dependent Hamiltonians. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and no global existence of canonical maps.

pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canon:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of [[def-cm13-poisson]] and the
canonical maps of [[def-cm13-canonical-map]]
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let $C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ be a $C^{2}$ canonical map
between nonempty open subsets of phase domains of the presentation, and let
$H:I_{0}\times W_{2}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$; write
$H\circ C$ for the function $(t,z)\mapsto H(t,C(z))$ on $I_{0}\times W_{1}$.
Then:

1. **(field transport)** For every $C^{2}$ function $f$ on $W_{2}$ and every
   $z\in W_{1}$,

$$DC(z)\,X_{f\circ C}(z)=X_{f}\bigl(C(z)\bigr),$$

   i.e. $C$ conjugates the Hamiltonian field of $f\circ C$ on $W_{1}$ to the
   field of $f$ on $W_{2}$.
2. **(bracket invariance)** For all $C^{2}$ functions $f,g$ on $W_{2}$,

$$\{f\circ C,\,g\circ C\}=\{f,g\}\circ C\qquad\text{on }W_{1},$$

   so the bracket of the presentation is invariant under canonical maps.
3. **(transport of solutions)** Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open
   interval and let $z:J\to W_{1}$ be a $C^{1}$ curve. Then $z$ solves
   $\dot z(t)=X_{(H\circ C)_{t}}(z(t))$ if and only if $t\mapsto C(z(t))$ solves
   $\dot w(t)=X_{H_{t}}(w(t))$ on $J$: the canonical map carries the
   Hamiltonian system of $H\circ C$ to that of $H$, with time dependence
   allowed.
4. **(instances)** In particular: the chart transitions of the presentation
   transport the Cartesian and generalized-coordinate Hamilton descriptions
   into one another; the time-slice maps of the flow-preservation
   theorem of this page transport the system to the system of
   $H\circ\Phi_{t}$; and the maps generated by first- and second-kind
   generating functions transport the system to the system of the transformed
   Hamiltonian.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and
no global existence of canonical maps.
lem-cm13-poincare-cartan-annihilation-ch:
## Statement

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let
$W\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open and nonempty with coordinates
$z=(q,p)=(q^{1},\dots,q^{n},p_{1},\dots,p_{n})$, and let
$H:J\times W\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{1}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). On the open set
$J\times W\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{2n}$ consider the two-form

$$\sigma:=d\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}p_{i}\,dq^{i}-H\,dt\Bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}dp_{i}\wedge dq^{i}-dH\wedge dt$$

([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]],
[[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]]). Let
$J'\subseteq J$ be a nonempty open interval and let $z:J'\to W$ be a $C^{1}$
curve. Then the following are equivalent:

1. $z$ satisfies Hamilton's equations on $J'$:
   $\dot q^{i}(t)=H_{p_{i}}\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)$ and
   $\dot p_{i}(t)=-H_{q^{i}}\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ and every
   $t\in J'$;
2. for every $t\in J'$ the covector
   $\iota_{(1,\dot z(t))}\sigma$ vanishes, that is
   $\sigma_{(t,z(t))}\bigl((1,\dot z(t)),w\bigr)=0$ for every
   $w\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{2n}$.

pthm-cm13-liouville.physical_scope: Phase-volume conservation for the declared potential presentation: the top form $\omega^{3N}/(3N)!$ is nowhere zero and is preserved by every time slice of the $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian evolution, and the Lebesgue measure of every canonical chart is preserved on bounded Borel sets of the actual flow domain, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics, and in its measure-theoretic part it uses the Axiom of Countable Choice exactly where the cited change-of-variables theorem requires it; no empirical content is asserted.

pthm-cm13-liouville:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), where the change-of-variables theorem below
requires it. Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and
mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the momentum charts and
two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical coordinates of
[[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the flow of [[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]]:
$H:I_{0}\times W\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ with
$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ on the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Write $n:=3N$ and let

$$\Omega:=\frac{1}{n!}\,\omega^{\wedge n}$$

be the **phase-volume form of the presentation**; by
[[cor-symplectic-manifolds-have-a-canonical-orientation-and-volume-form]]
applied to the symplectic phase domain of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]], $\Omega$ is a nowhere-zero top form
of the canonical charts, and by
[[prop-pullback-of-forms-is-smooth-functorial-and-preserves-wedges]] it is
pulled back to itself by every canonical map. Let $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $z_{0}\in
W$ and let $\Phi_{t}=\Phi(t;\cdot)$ be the time-$t$ solution map of the
Hamiltonian system on the neighbourhood $U_{0}$ supplied by
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]], with image
$V_{t}:=\Phi_{t}(U_{0})$. Then:

1. **(form preservation)** For every $t$ on the existence interval,
   $\Phi_{t}^{*}\Omega=\Omega$ on $U_{0}$; the time slices of the model's
   Hamiltonian evolution preserve the phase-volume form.
2. **(measure preservation)** For every $t$ on the existence interval and
   every bounded Borel set $A\subseteq U_{0}$ with
   $\overline A\subseteq U_{0}$, the sets $A$ and $\Phi_{t}(A)$ are
   Lebesgue measurable and

$$\lambda_{6N}\bigl(\Phi_{t}(A)\bigr)=\lambda_{6N}(A),$$

   where $\lambda_{6N}$ is the Lebesgue measure of the chart
   ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
   [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]],
   [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]).
3. **(chart independence)** The measure statement is independent of the
   canonical chart: for two canonical charts with transition $\Theta$ and
   Borel sets of finite measure, $\lambda(\Theta(B))=\lambda(B)$ on the
   overlap, because the transition has $|\det D\Theta|=1$
   ([[def-cm13-canonical-form]],
   [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]).
4. **(potential branch)** On the potential branch ($d\equiv0$) the time
   slices are the momentum-phase maps of the model's motions
   ([[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]), so the
   model's Hamiltonian evolution conserves phase volume on its actual
   domains; no completeness and no all-time statement is claimed.

pthm-cm13-generating-functions.physical_scope: Generating-function theory for the declared potential presentation: first- and second-kind generating functions of the model's canonical charts generate canonical local diffeomorphisms of the presentation with the recorded one-form identities and unit determinant; a canonical diffeomorphism with invertible $(q,Q)$-projection is locally generated in the first kind; and for a time-dependent generating function the transformed Hamiltonian is $K=H+S_t$, with the Hamilton systems of $H$ and $K$ carried into one another by the generated time-dependent map. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global generating function and no empirical content.

pthm-cm13-generating-functions:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Write $n':=3N$ and let $O_{q},O_{Q},O_{P}\subseteq
Q$-coordinates and $\mathbb R^{n'}$ be as below. Then:

1. **(first kind)** Let $S:O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$
   with $\det S_{qQ}(q,Q)\neq0$ everywhere
   ([[def-cm-generating-function-of-the-first-and-second-kind]]), and define
   the **local map generated by $S$** by solving $p=S_{q}(q,Q)$ for
   $Q=Q(q,p)$ and setting $P:=-S_{Q}(q,Q)$: a $C^{2}$ map
   $C:(q,p)\mapsto(Q,P)$ defined on a neighbourhood of each point of the
   solution set. Then $C$ is a canonical $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism of the
   presentation: $DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$, $C^{*}\omega=\omega$ and
   $|\det DC|=1$; and the one-form identity $p\cdot dq-P\cdot dQ=dS$ holds on
   the $(q,Q)$-domain ([[prop-cm-generating-functions-yield-canonical-maps]]).
2. **(second kind)** Let $S:O_{q}\times O_{P}\to\mathbb R$ be $C^{3}$ with
   $\det S_{qP}\neq0$ everywhere, and define the local map by
   $p=S_{q}(q,P)$, $Q=S_{P}(q,P)$. Then it is again a canonical $C^{2}$ local
   diffeomorphism of the presentation with the recorded identity
   $p\cdot dq+Q\cdot dP=dS$.
3. **(local converse)** Let $C$ be a $C^{2}$ canonical diffeomorphism between
   nonempty open subsets of the presentation's Cartesian phase domains, and
   suppose that the projection $z\mapsto(q(z),Q(z))$ onto the old position
   and the new position has invertible derivative at a point $z_{0}$. Then
   there are a neighbourhood of $z_{0}$ and a $C^{3}$ function
   $S:O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$ with $\det S_{qQ}\neq0$ whose generated
   map agrees with $C$ on that neighbourhood
   ([[prop-cm-canonical-map-locally-has-a-generating-function]]).
4. **(time-dependent generating function)** Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a
   nonempty open interval and let $S:J\times O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$
   be of class $C^{3}$ with $\det S_{qQ}(t,q,Q)\neq0$ everywhere; for each
   $t$ let $C_{t}$ be the first-kind map generated by $S_{t}$. Assume the
   values $(q,p)$ used below lie in the domain of $H$ of
   [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], and set
   $p:=S_{q}(t,q,Q)$, $P:=-S_{Q}(t,q,Q)$ and
   $K(t,q,Q):=H\bigl(t,q,S_{q}(t,q,Q)\bigr)+S_{t}(t,q,Q)$. Then:
   (a) each $C_{t}$ is a canonical $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism of the
   presentation; (b) the Poincare-Cartan identity

$$p\cdot dq-H\,dt=P\cdot dQ-K\,dt+dS$$

   holds on $J\times O_{q}\times O_{Q}$
   ([[prop-cm-time-dependent-generating-function]]); and (c) writing $K$ as
   a function of $(t,Q,P)$ through the correspondence
   $(t,q,Q)\leftrightarrow(t,Q,P)$, a $C^{1}$ curve $t\mapsto(q(t),p(t))$
   satisfies $q'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{q}$ if and only if
   $t\mapsto(Q(t),P(t))=C_{t}(q(t),p(t))$ satisfies $Q'=K_{P}$,
   $P'=-K_{Q}$ on the interval where both descriptions are defined.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global generating
function, no existence of a canonical map with prescribed data beyond the
local statements, and no empirical content.
